Cause Typical foods Symptoms start Staphylococcus aureus toxin Food handled by hand then left out: pastries, sandwiches, kuih, cooked meats 30 minutes to 8 hours (usually 2 to 4) Bacillus cereus Cooked rice and noodles left at room temperature, such as nasi lemak, fried rice and buffet rice 1 to 6 hours (vomiting) or 6 to 24 hours (diarrhoea) Vibrio Raw or undercooked shellfish and seafood 4 to 30 hours Norovirus Contaminated food or water, or contact with someone ill 12 to 48 hours Salmonella Undercooked chicken and eggs, foods made with raw egg 6 to 48 hours Campylobacter Undercooked chicken, unpasteurised milk 2 to 5 days Some types of E. coli Undercooked beef, raw vegetables, unclean water 3 to 4 days Rice is a common culprit. Bacillus cereus spores survive cooking and multiply in rice left warm. Its toxin isn’t destroyed by reheating, so rice that has been left out for hours isn’t made safe by heating it up. Gastroenteritis (a “stomach bug” or “stomach flu”) is often caused by viruses such as norovirus, and in young children rotavirus, and spreads easily from person to person. It has nothing to do with influenza. The rotavirus vaccine isn’t part of the National Immunisation Programme but is available at private clinics: see our baby vaccination schedule . A fever lasting several days after eating out may be typhoid rather than ordinary food poisoning. See our guide to the typhoid injection . nausea and vomiting diarrhoea (cirit-birit) tummy cramps fever, aches and feeling generally unwell Vomiting usually stops within 1 to 2 days and diarrhoea within 5 to 7 days. Most people recover within a week. You can pass a stomach bug on for at least 2 days after the diarrhoea and vomiting stop, so stay home from work or school until then. Severe, constant tummy pain, especially if it moves to the lower right side, may be something else, such as appendicitis. See our guides to stomach pain and appendicitis . Diarrhoea and vomiting drain the body of water and salts. Oral rehydration salts (ORS) , sold in sachets at pharmacies, contain the right balance of salts and sugar to replace them: Mix each sachet with the amount of clean, boiled and cooled water stated on the pack, often 250 ml. Don’t make it stronger or weaker. Take small, frequent sips , especially if you are vomiting. Try a sip every few minutes, and keep going even if you vomit. Drink extra after each loose stool. Avoid fizzy drinks, fruit juice and very sweet drinks , which can make diarrhoea worse. Sports drinks aren’t a substitute for ORS for children. Babies: keep breastfeeding or giving formula as usual, with ORS between feeds if advised. Eating: start eating normally as soon as you feel able, with plain foods such as rice, porridge (bubur), bread, bananas and soup. There is no need to stop eating for long. Wash raw vegetables in clean water, and keep raw meat and seafood away from foods that won’t be cooked. Paracetamol helps with fever and aches. Anti-diarrhoea medicine (loperamide) can reduce diarrhoea for a few hours in adults, for example for travel. Don’t use it if you have blood or mucus in your stool or a high fever , and don’t give it to children under 12. Antibiotics usually aren’t needed and don’t help viral gastroenteritis. A doctor may prescribe them for some bacterial infections, such as severe or bloody diarrhoea. Probiotics probably make little or no difference to how long diarrhoea lasts, according to a Cochrane review. Activated charcoal has little evidence for diarrhoea and can stop other medicines from working. Ask a pharmacist or doctor before giving any medicine to a baby or young child. See a doctor if: there is blood in the diarrhoea or vomit you have a high fever (38.9°C or above) you can’t keep fluids down because of vomiting diarrhoea lasts more than 3 days in adults, or vomiting lasts more than 2 days you have signs of dehydration : passing very little urine, very dark urine, dry mouth, dizziness when standing the person ill is a baby under 1 year , an older person, pregnant, or has diabetes, kidney disease or a weak immune system Go to an emergency department, or call 999 , if: a child is very drowsy or floppy, has sunken eyes, is drinking poorly, or has far fewer wet nappies than usual there is green or bloody vomit, or severe, sudden tummy pain someone is confused, or faints See our guide on clinic or emergency department . During and after floods, diarrhoea can also come from contaminated water: see our guide to floods and your health . The World Health Organization’s Five Keys to Safer Food : Keep clean: wash your hands with soap for at least 20 seconds before handling food and after using the toilet. Separate raw and cooked: use separate boards and knives for raw meat, chicken and seafood. Cook thoroughly: especially chicken, eggs and seafood, until piping hot. Keep food at safe temperatures: don’t leave cooked food at room temperature for more than 2 hours, or 1 hour in very hot weather. Keep hot food hot and cold food cold, and refrigerate leftovers quickly. Use safe water and raw materials: boil or treat drinking water if unsure, and wash fruit and vegetables. At kenduri, buffets and events, be wary of rice, curries and kuih that have been sitting out for hours. If you have diarrhoea or vomiting, don’t prepare food for others until 48 hours after your symptoms stop. How long does food poisoning last? Usually a few days. Vomiting often stops within 1 to 2 days and diarrhoea within 5 to 7 days. Most people recover within a week. How soon after eating does food poisoning start? Anywhere from 30 minutes to several days. Toxins in food left out, such as rice, can cause vomiting within 1 to 6 hours, while Salmonella usually takes 6 to 48 hours. What is the best drink for diarrhoea? Oral rehydration salts (ORS) mixed with clean water as directed on the pack. Avoid fizzy drinks and fruit juice. Should I take antibiotics for food poisoning? Usually not. Most food poisoning and stomach bugs get better without them. A doctor will prescribe antibiotics if they are needed. Can I take anti-diarrhoea medicine? Adults can take loperamide for a short time, but not if there is blood in the stool or a high fever. It isn’t for children under 12. When should I see a doctor for diarrhoea? If there is blood, high fever, signs of dehydration, vomiting that stops you keeping fluids down, diarrhoea lasting more than 3 days, or if a baby, older person or pregnant woman is ill. What is the difference between food poisoning and gastroenteritis? Gastroenteritis is inflammation of the stomach and gut, often caused by viruses that spread between people. Food poisoning is illness caused by contaminated food. The symptoms are similar. Is reheated rice safe? Only if it was cooled quickly and kept in the fridge. Rice left warm for hours can grow Bacillus cereus, whose toxin isn’t destroyed by reheating.

title: Kurap, panau and other fungal skin infections: how to recognise and treat them
desc: Malaysia’s heat and humidity make fungal skin infections very common. How to recognise kurap (ringworm), panau, athlete’s foot, jock itch and scalp ringworm, how long to use antifungal cream, why steroid creams make it worse, and when you need a doctor.
headings: Types of fungal skin infection · How kurap spreads · Treatment for kurap (ubat kurap) · Why steroid creams make kurap worse · Treating panau · Preventing fungal infections · When to see a doctor
keywords: Aesthetics & skin Kurap and panau Tinea Kurap Pityriasis versicolor kencing manis gula hba1c payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Kurap (ringworm, or tinea) is caused by fungi, not worms. It usually looks like an itchy, red or dark ring with a scaly, raised edge and a clearer centre. Panau (pityriasis versicolor) causes pale, pink or brown scaly patches on the chest, back, neck and arms. It is caused by a yeast that lives on everyone’s skin and isn’t contagious. Antifungal creams such as clotrimazole, miconazole or terbinafine work for most body, groin and foot infections. Keep using them for 1 to 2 weeks after the rash has gone. Steroid creams and steroid-antifungal combination creams can make kurap spread. A treatment-resistant fungus linked to steroid cream misuse has now been found in Malaysia. Scalp and nail infections, and rashes that don’t clear in 2 weeks, need a doctor, as they often need antifungal tablets. Infection Where What it looks like Ringworm of the body (tinea corporis, kurap ) Body, arms, legs, face An itchy ring or round patch with a scaly, raised edge and a clearer centre. Red on lighter skin, grey or brown on darker skin Jock itch (tinea cruris) Groin and inner thighs An itchy, red-brown rash with a clear edge Athlete’s foot (tinea pedis) Between the toes, soles Itchy, white, cracked or peeling skin, sometimes blisters Scalp ringworm (tinea capitis) Scalp, mostly children aged 3 to 7 Scaly patches with broken hair or hair loss, sometimes a painful, swollen, pus-filled lump (kerion) Fungal nail infection Mostly toenails Thick, discoloured, crumbly nails Panau (pityriasis versicolor) Chest, back, neck, upper arms Pale, pink or light brown patches with fine scale, more noticeable after sun Candida (yeast) intertrigo Skin folds: groin, under the breasts, armpits Moist, red, raw skin with small spots at the edges Kayap isn’t a fungal infection. It is shingles, caused by the chickenpox virus, and needs different treatment. See our guide to shingles (kayap) . Kurap is caused by fungi called dermatophytes, which live on skin, hair and nails. It spreads through: skin contact with an infected person, for example in contact sports sharing towels, clothes, bedding, shoes or socks damp floors in gyms, changing rooms and shared bathrooms pets , especially cats and kittens. A Hospital Melaka study found that a fungus caught from cats caused more than half of scalp ringworm cases. Take a pet with scaly or hairless patches to the vet ( kurap kucing can pass to people). Heat, sweat, tight clothes and shoes, diabetes and a weak immune system all make infection more likely. It usually appears 1 to 3 weeks after contact. Panau is different. It is caused by an overgrowth of Malassezia , a yeast that normally lives on everyone’s skin. It flares in heat and sweat and isn’t passed from person to person in the usual way. For kurap on the body, groin or feet, a pharmacist can recommend an antifungal cream such as clotrimazole, miconazole or terbinafine: Wash and dry the area well, then apply the cream thinly to the rash and about 2 cm of normal skin around it, usually once or twice a day. Keep using it for 1 to 2 weeks after the rash has gone. Stopping as soon as it looks better is a common reason it comes back. Most rashes improve within 2 weeks. Treatment can take up to 4 weeks. Treat athlete’s foot at the same time as jock itch, as the fungus spreads from the feet to the groin, often via a towel or underwear. Antifungal tablets , prescribed by a doctor, are needed for scalp ringworm (creams can’t reach the hair roots), most nail infections, widespread rashes, and infections that haven’t cleared with cream. Scalp ringworm usually needs at least 4 weeks of tablets, and nail infections up to 6 months. Steroid creams calm itching and redness, so kurap can seem better at first. But they weaken the skin’s defences and let the fungus spread underneath, leaving a larger, less typical rash that is harder to recognise and treat. Doctors call this tinea incognito . Combination creams containing both an antifungal and a steroid are sold over the counter in Malaysia. Reviews have found they don’t cure the fungus any better than an antifungal alone, so use them only if a doctor advises. In 2025, researchers at Universiti Malaya reported Malaysia’s first confirmed cases of Trichophyton indotineae , a fungus behind an epidemic of widespread, treatment-resistant ringworm in South Asia that has been linked to steroid cream misuse. Some of the Malaysian patients had not travelled abroad and had used steroid creams, and some responded poorly to standard treatment. Check that creams and traditional remedies are registered with the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA). Registered products carry a MAL number . The Ministry of Health has repeatedly warned about unregistered products found to contain hidden steroids. If you are unsure whether a rash is fungal, see a doctor before using a steroid cream. Our guide to itchy skin explains the safe use of steroid creams for eczema. Use an antifungal shampoo or wash containing ketoconazole or selenium sulfide on the affected skin. Leave it on for 5 to 15 minutes, then rinse. A common routine is daily for a week, then once a week for a month. Antifungal creams work for small areas. The colour takes weeks to months to return after the yeast has gone, especially pale patches. That doesn’t mean the treatment failed. Sun exposure makes the patches more noticeable. Panau often comes back in hot weather. Using the wash once or twice a month can help prevent it. See a doctor if it is widespread or keeps coming back. Antifungal tablets are sometimes used. Dry your skin thoroughly after bathing, especially between the toes, in the groin and in skin folds. Change out of sweaty clothes and socks promptly, and wear loose cotton clothing and socks. Don’t share towels, clothes, shoes, combs or hats. Use your own towel for your feet. Wear slippers in shared showers, gyms and changing rooms. Wash gym clothes and towels after each use. Check pets for patchy hair loss, and wash your hands after handling them. Damp gym floors and sweaty clothes are a common source of kurap and athlete’s foot. the rash hasn’t improved after 2 weeks of antifungal cream, or keeps coming back it is on the scalp , or affects the nails it is widespread, or you have used a steroid cream on it you have diabetes or a weak immune system the skin becomes hot, swollen and painful, or you have a fever, which can mean a bacterial infection you aren’t sure it is fungal. Eczema, psoriasis and other rashes can look like ringworm. See our guide to psoriasis . A doctor can often tell by looking, and may gently scrape some scale to test for fungus. For an intensely itchy rash that is worse at night and affects others at home, see our guide to scabies (kudis buta) . What is kurap in English? Kurap is ringworm, a fungal skin infection also called tinea. Despite the name, it isn’t caused by a worm. How long does kurap take to go away? Most cases improve within 2 weeks of using an antifungal cream. Keep using it for 1 to 2 weeks after the rash has gone, which can mean up to 4 weeks in total. Can I use a steroid cream on kurap? No, unless a doctor advises it. Steroid creams can make kurap spread and harder to treat, and have been linked to treatment-resistant ringworm. Is panau contagious? No. Panau is caused by a yeast that normally lives on everyone’s skin. It flares in heat and sweat, but isn’t passed between people in the usual way. Why are my panau patches still white after treatment? Skin colour takes weeks to months to return after the yeast has been treated. It doesn’t mean the treatment failed. Can I get kurap from my cat? Yes. Cats and kittens can carry a fungus that causes ringworm in people, especially scalp ringworm in children. Take the pet to a vet and see a doctor for the rash. When does kurap need tablets? For scalp and nail infections, widespread rashes, and infections that haven’t cleared with cream. A doctor can prescribe antifungal tablets. Is kayap a fungal infection? No. Kayap is shingles, caused by the chickenpox virus. It needs antiviral treatment, not antifungal cream.

title: Blood test results explained: FBC, CRP, ESR, liver and kidney tests, and what a check-up includes
desc: Got your blood test report and not sure what the numbers mean? A plain-language guide to the full blood count, CRP and ESR, liver and kidney tests, which tests need fasting, what a typical medical check-up includes, and where to get screened free in Malaysia.
headings: Full blood count (FBC) · CRP and ESR: inflammation markers · Liver function tests (LFT) · Kidney function tests · Other common tests · Do I need to fast before a blood test? · What a medical check-up includes, and free options
keywords: Guides Blood test results explained Blood test Full blood count Health screening denggi aedes nyamuk mosquito kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: Reference ranges differ between labs. A result slightly outside the range is often normal for you, so look at the whole picture with a doctor. Small red blood cells (low MCV) are common in Malaysia and can mean iron deficiency or thalassaemia trait, which need different treatment. Raised liver enzymes (ALT) are most often caused by fatty liver, which affects about 3 in 10 Malaysian adults. About 1 in 7 Malaysian adults has chronic kidney disease, and only 1 in 20 of them knows. People with diabetes or high blood pressure should have yearly kidney tests. STR recipients aged 40 and over can get free blood tests through PeKa B40, and eligible PERKESO contributors aged 40 to 59 through its health screening programme. The full blood count (FBC, or full blood picture) measures the cells in your blood. Test Typical adult range What it can mean Haemoglobin (Hb) Men about 130–180 g/L; women about 115–165 g/L Low: anaemia , for example from iron deficiency, heavy periods, blood loss or thalassaemia MCV and MCH (red cell size) MCV about 80–100 fL; MCH about 27–32 pg Low: iron deficiency or thalassaemia trait . High: low vitamin B12 or folate, alcohol, liver disease White cells (WBC) About 4–11 ×10⁹/L High: infection, inflammation, steroids, rarely leukaemia. Low: some viral infections (such as dengue), medicines Platelets About 150–400 ×10⁹/L Low: higher bleeding risk, for example in dengue . High: inflammation, iron deficiency Haemoglobin is sometimes reported in g/dL: divide g/L by 10 (so 130 g/L is 13.0 g/dL). Small red cells are common in Malaysia. They can mean iron deficiency, which is treated with iron, or thalassaemia trait, which isn’t, and iron tablets don’t help. A doctor can check your iron levels and arrange a thalassaemia test. See our guide to thalassaemia screening . CRP (C-reactive protein) is made by the liver when there is inflammation or infection, and rises within hours. A normal result is usually below about 5 to 10 mg/L, depending on the lab. Very high levels often point to a bacterial infection. ESR (erythrocyte sedimentation rate) measures how fast red cells settle in a tube in an hour. It rises more slowly than CRP and is naturally higher in women, older people, pregnancy and anaemia. Typical upper limits are around 15 to 20 mm/hr for men and 20 to 30 mm/hr for women, depending on age. Both are signals, not diagnoses : they show that inflammation is present, but not where or why. Doctors use them alongside your symptoms and other tests, and to check whether a condition is improving. A high-sensitivity CRP (hs-CRP) is a different test sometimes used to assess heart disease risk. Test What it shows ALT and AST Enzymes released when liver cells are damaged. ALT is the more liver-specific of the two ALP and GGT Raised in bile duct problems. GGT also rises with alcohol and some medicines. ALP also comes from bone Bilirubin A yellow pigment. High levels cause jaundice. Mildly raised bilirubin on its own is often harmless (Gilbert’s syndrome) Albumin A protein made by the liver. Low levels can mean long-term liver disease, kidney problems or poor nutrition Common causes of raised ALT in Malaysia: fatty liver (now called MASLD or MAFLD). A 2023 Ministry of Health survey found it in 28.2% of adults , about 6.7 million people, including 1 in 5 adults aged 18 to 29. It is linked to excess weight, diabetes and high cholesterol. See our BMI calculator . alcohol hepatitis B and C . See our guide to hepatitis B . medicines, and herbal or slimming supplements a recent illness or very hard exercise, which can cause short-lived rises Mildly raised results are often rechecked after a few weeks, and the doctor may arrange a liver ultrasound. Creatinine is a waste product from muscles, cleared by the kidneys. A high level suggests the kidneys aren’t filtering well. eGFR (estimated glomerular filtration rate) is calculated from creatinine, age and sex. It estimates how well your kidneys filter, in mL/min/1.73m². Urea is another waste product, affected by dehydration and diet as well as kidney function. Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR or UACR) detects protein leaking into the urine, an early sign of kidney damage, especially in diabetes. Stage eGFR Meaning G1 90 or more Normal filtering. Counts as kidney disease only with other signs of damage, such as protein in the urine G2 60–89 Mildly reduced. Common with age. Kidney disease only with other signs of damage G3a / G3b 45–59 / 30–44 Moderately reduced G4 15–29 Severely reduced G5 Below 15 Kidney failure Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is diagnosed when results stay abnormal for more than 3 months. In Malaysia, a national survey found CKD in 15.5% of adults in 2018, up from 9.1% in 2011, but only about 5% of those affected knew. About 50,000 people were on dialysis in 2023, with more than 10,000 starting each year. High blood pressure and diabetes are the main causes, so people with either should have their kidney blood and urine tests at least once a year. Test What it checks Read more Fasting glucose and HbA1c Diabetes and prediabetes Normal blood sugar levels Lipid profile (cholesterol, LDL, HDL, triglycerides) Heart disease and stroke risk Blood pressure and cholesterol Uric acid Gout and kidney stones Gout TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone) Overactive or underactive thyroid Thyroid problems Urine test (urine FEME) Sugar, protein, blood and signs of infection UTI Fasting glucose needs a fast of at least 8 hours, usually overnight. Cholesterol tests often don’t need fasting now, but some labs and doctors still ask for a 10 to 12 hour fast, mainly because triglycerides rise after eating. Follow the instructions you are given. HbA1c, the full blood count, and liver and kidney tests usually don’t need fasting. When fasting, you can drink plain water . Avoid tea, coffee, sweet drinks and chewing gum. Take your usual medicines unless told otherwise, but ask about diabetes medicines and insulin, which may need adjusting while you fast. Stop biotin supplements (often in hair and nail products) 2 days before, as they can distort some results, including thyroid tests. Fasting glucose needs an overnight fast. HbA1c and most other tests don’t. A typical health screening includes a consultation, blood pressure, weight and waist measurement, and blood and urine tests such as: full blood count fasting glucose or HbA1c lipid profile kidney function (creatinine, eGFR) and urine test liver function, and sometimes uric acid, thyroid and hepatitis B tests Free and low-cost options: PeKa B40: STR recipients and their spouses aged 40 and over get free tests at panel clinics: full blood count, kidney profile with eGFR, HbA1c, lipid profile and urine tests, with no fasting needed and a second visit to explain the results. See our PeKa B40 guide . PERKESO Health Screening Programme: eligible Malaysian contributors aged 40 to 59 get free blood and urine tests at panel clinics. Klinik Kesihatan: basic screening for a minimal fee. Private clinics and labs: packages range from under RM100 to several hundred ringgit, depending on the tests included. See our guide to free health screening in Malaysia . Whichever you choose, have a doctor go through your results , especially any flagged as high or low, rather than relying on the report alone. What does a full blood count check? Your red cells (including haemoglobin and cell size), white cells and platelets. It can show anaemia, infection, inflammation and bleeding risks. What is a normal CRP level? Usually below about 5 to 10 mg/L, depending on the lab. A raised CRP shows inflammation or infection but not the cause. What does a high ALT mean? Liver cells may be inflamed or damaged. In Malaysia the most common cause is fatty liver, but alcohol, hepatitis B or C and medicines are also possible. A doctor may repeat the test and arrange an ultrasound. What is a normal eGFR? 90 or above is normal, and 60 to 89 can be normal, especially with age. Below 60 for more than 3 months means chronic kidney disease. Do I need to fast before a blood test? Only for some tests, mainly fasting glucose and sometimes cholesterol. Drink plain water and take your usual medicines unless told otherwise. Why does my report show results outside the normal range? Ranges cover about 95% of healthy people, so slightly abnormal results are common and often not significant. A doctor will look at the whole picture. Where can I get a free blood test in Malaysia? Through PeKa B40 if you receive STR and are 40 or over, and through PERKESO’s screening programme if you are an eligible contributor aged 40 to 59. Klinik Kesihatan offer basic screening for a minimal fee. How often should I have a blood test? It depends on your age and health. Adults are generally advised to screen for diabetes, cholesterol and kidney problems regularly from 30 or 40, and every year if you have diabetes or high blood pressure. Ask your doctor.

title: Thyroid problems in Malaysia: overactive and underactive thyroid, goitre and the thyroid blood test
desc: Thyroid problems are the second most common hormone disorder in Malaysia after diabetes, and most people who have one don’t know it. The signs of an overactive and underactive thyroid, goitre and lumps, what the thyroid blood test shows, and how they are treated.
headings: Thyroid problems in Malaysia · Overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism) · Underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism) · The thyroid blood test · Goitre, thyroid lumps and iodine · Thyroid problems and pregnancy · Thyroid and weight
keywords: Weight & metabolism Thyroid problems Thyroid disease Hyperthyroidism Hypothyroidism kencing manis gula hba1c payudara kanser cancer mammogram pink october mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: A nationwide Malaysian study found that about 3 in 100 adults had an overactive thyroid and 2 in 100 an underactive one, counting mild cases, and that most had never been diagnosed. An overactive thyroid (hyperthyroidism) causes weight loss, a fast heartbeat, shaking, sweating and anxiety. An underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism) causes tiredness, feeling cold, constipation and weight gain. The main test is TSH. A high TSH usually means an underactive thyroid, and a low TSH an overactive one. If you take anti-thyroid tablets and get a sore throat, mouth ulcers or fever, stop them and get an urgent blood count. Most thyroid lumps are harmless, but any new or growing lump should be checked. Malaysia has required table salt to be iodised since 2020 to prevent goitre. Thyroid disorders are the second most common hormone (endocrine) disorder in Malaysia after diabetes. In a nationwide study of more than 2,200 adults, reported when Malaysia launched its first clinical practice guidelines on thyroid disorders in 2020: about 3.4% had an overactive thyroid and 2.1% an underactive one, including mild (subclinical) cases 9.3% had a goitre (an enlarged thyroid) and 3.6% had nodules (lumps) most of those with an abnormal thyroid had never been diagnosed Thyroid problems are much more common in women , and often start between the ages of 20 and 40, or after pregnancy. Symptoms: weight loss despite a good appetite fast or irregular heartbeat (palpitations) shaky hands, sweating and feeling hot anxiety, irritability and poor sleep loose stools, lighter or fewer periods a swelling in the neck (goitre) gritty, red or bulging eyes, or double vision (thyroid eye disease) Causes: about 4 in 5 cases are due to Graves’ disease , an autoimmune condition. Others are caused by overactive thyroid nodules, or by inflammation of the thyroid (thyroiditis), which is often temporary, including after pregnancy. Treatment: Beta-blockers to ease palpitations and shaking while other treatment takes effect. Anti-thyroid tablets (carbimazole, methimazole or, in early pregnancy, propylthiouracil), usually for 12 to 18 months. Radioactive iodine , a drink or capsule that shrinks the thyroid. It isn’t used in pregnancy or breastfeeding, and can worsen thyroid eye disease. Surgery to remove the thyroid, for example for a large goitre. Taking anti-thyroid tablets? Rarely, they lower the white blood cells that fight infection. If you get a sore throat, mouth ulcers, fever or flu-like illness , stop the tablets and see a doctor the same day for a blood count. Smoking makes thyroid eye disease worse, so it is especially important to stop. Symptoms come on slowly and are easy to blame on stress or age: tiredness and sluggishness feeling cold weight gain, usually modest constipation dry skin and hair, hair thinning low mood, poor memory heavier or irregular periods, and difficulty getting pregnant Causes: most often the autoimmune condition Hashimoto’s thyroiditis . Others include previous thyroid surgery or radioactive iodine, some medicines (such as lithium and amiodarone), and iodine deficiency. Treatment is a daily levothyroxine tablet, which replaces the missing hormone: Take it at the same time each day, on an empty stomach, 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast. Keep it at least 4 hours apart from calcium, iron and antacids , which stop it being absorbed. Your TSH is rechecked 6 to 8 weeks after starting or changing the dose, then usually once a year once it is stable. Subclinical hypothyroidism , a raised TSH with normal thyroid hormone, is common and often settles without treatment. Doctors usually repeat the test before deciding on treatment. Test What it shows TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone) The main screening test. High usually means an underactive thyroid; low usually means an overactive one. A typical range is about 0.4 to 4.5 mIU/L, but check your lab’s range Free T4 (and sometimes free T3) The thyroid hormones themselves, to confirm and measure the problem TPO antibodies Point to Hashimoto’s thyroiditis TSH receptor antibodies (TRAb) Point to Graves’ disease You don’t need to fast. Stop biotin supplements, found in many hair and nail products, 2 days before the test, as biotin can give falsely abnormal results. Ask for a thyroid test if you have symptoms above, a goitre, a family history of thyroid disease, other autoimmune conditions such as type 1 diabetes, irregular periods or difficulty conceiving, or are planning a pregnancy with a past thyroid problem. See also our guide to blood test results . A TSH blood test is the simplest way to check your thyroid. A goitre is an enlarged thyroid, seen as a swelling at the front of the neck. A nodule is a lump within the thyroid. Thyroid nodules are very common : about half of people have one by age 60, and more than 9 in 10 are harmless. They are checked with an ultrasound , and if needed a fine-needle biopsy. See a doctor promptly for a lump that is growing, or a lump with a hoarse voice, difficulty swallowing or breathing. Thyroid cancer is the 8th most common cancer in Malaysian women. Most are the papillary type, which, found early, has a 10-year survival of nearly 100%. Iodine: the thyroid needs iodine to make its hormones. Iodine deficiency has long caused goitre in parts of Malaysia, especially interior Sabah and Sarawak. A national survey found nearly half of children aged 8 to 10 were iodine deficient, so since the end of 2020, table and fine salt sold in packs of up to 20 kg must be iodised . In Sarawak, goitre in children fell from 2.9% in 2008 to 0.1% in 2018 after salt iodisation. Use iodised salt at home, but don’t take extra iodine supplements unless advised, as too much can also upset the thyroid. Untreated thyroid problems raise the risk of miscarriage, pre-eclampsia and premature birth, and an underactive thyroid can affect the baby’s brain development. If you take levothyroxine , the dose usually needs to go up by 20 to 30% as soon as you are pregnant. Tell your doctor straight away and have your TSH checked, then about every 4 weeks in the first half of pregnancy. If you have an overactive thyroid , your doctor may switch your medicine before or early in pregnancy. Radioactive iodine must not be used. Newborn screening: babies born in Malaysia are tested for congenital hypothyroidism using blood from the umbilical cord, so that it can be treated before it affects development. See our pregnancy week-by-week guide . An underactive thyroid usually adds only a few kilograms, much of it fluid, and this tends to come off with treatment. If you have gained a lot of weight, the thyroid is rarely the only cause. Thyroid hormone shouldn’t be used for weight loss : it can cause heart rhythm problems and bone loss, and the weight returns. See our BMI calculator and guide to weight-loss injections . What are the symptoms of thyroid problems? An overactive thyroid causes weight loss, palpitations, shaking, sweating and anxiety. An underactive thyroid causes tiredness, feeling cold, constipation, dry skin and weight gain. What is the difference between hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism? Hyperthyroidism means the thyroid makes too much hormone, speeding the body up. Hypothyroidism means it makes too little, slowing the body down. What does a high TSH mean? Usually that your thyroid is underactive, as the pituitary gland is working harder to stimulate it. A doctor will check your free T4 to confirm. Is a goitre dangerous? Most goitres and thyroid lumps are harmless, but they should be checked, especially if growing, or with a hoarse voice or difficulty swallowing or breathing. Do I need to fast for a thyroid blood test? No. But stop biotin supplements 2 days before, as they can affect the result. Is thyroid disease curable? An overactive thyroid can often be cured with tablets, radioactive iodine or surgery, although some people then need levothyroxine. An underactive thyroid is usually lifelong but well controlled with a daily tablet. Can thyroid problems cause weight gain? An underactive thyroid can cause modest weight gain, which usually improves with treatment. Large weight gain is rarely due to the thyroid alone. Why is salt iodised in Malaysia? To prevent iodine deficiency, which causes goitre and can affect children’s development. Since the end of 2020, table salt sold in packs of up to 20 kg must be iodised.

title: Urinary tract infection (UTI): symptoms, treatment, kidney infection signs and stopping it coming back
desc: Burning when you pass urine, needing to go often, cloudy or bloody urine: the signs of a urinary tract infection. Who needs to see a doctor, the warning signs of a kidney infection, how UTIs are treated in Malaysia, and what actually helps prevent them coming back.
headings: What is a UTI? · UTI symptoms · Warning signs of a kidney infection · How a UTI is diagnosed · UTI treatment · Preventing UTIs from coming back · UTIs in men, and “kencing tak lawas”
keywords: Women's health Urinary tract infection (UTI) Urinary tract infection Cystitis Jangkitan saluran kencing kencing manis gula hba1c mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp
body: Typical UTI symptoms are pain or burning when passing urine, needing to go often and urgently, cloudy or bloody urine, and lower tummy pain. Fever, shivering, pain in the back or side, or vomiting can mean a kidney infection, which needs a doctor the same day. Men, pregnant women, children, older people and people with diabetes or a catheter should always see a doctor for a UTI. In Malaysia, antibiotics need a doctor’s prescription. Common UTI bacteria are increasingly resistant to some antibiotics, so a urine culture is used for repeat or complicated infections. Drinking enough water and not holding urine help. Cranberry products modestly reduce repeat UTIs in some women. Vaginal oestrogen helps after the menopause. A UTI is an infection anywhere in the urinary tract, usually caused by bacteria from the gut, most often E. coli , getting into the urethra. Bladder infection (cystitis) is the most common type. Kidney infection (pyelonephritis) is less common but more serious. Women are much more likely to get UTIs because the urethra is shorter and closer to the back passage. Risk is higher after sex, in pregnancy, after the menopause, and with a previous UTI. Other risk factors include diabetes (some diabetes medicines, called SGLT2 inhibitors, also raise the risk of genital infections), kidney stones, a urinary catheter, not drinking enough, constipation in children, and in men, an enlarged prostate that stops the bladder emptying fully. pain, burning or stinging when passing urine ( sakit kencing ) needing to pass urine more often or urgently, including at night cloudy urine, or blood in the urine pain or pressure in the lower tummy feeling generally unwell or tired In older people , a UTI may cause new confusion, agitation, falls or worsening incontinence rather than typical symptoms. In children , look for fever, irritability, poor feeding, vomiting, tummy pain or new bedwetting. A baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C or more needs to see a doctor straight away. Dark or strong-smelling urine on its own usually means you need to drink more, not an infection. Vaginal itching or discharge points to another cause, such as thrush or a sexually transmitted infection. See our guide to STI testing . See a doctor the same day if you have UTI symptoms with: a high temperature, or shivering and shaking pain in your back or side, below the ribs feeling sick or vomiting Go to an emergency department if you are confused, very drowsy, have difficulty speaking, have passed no urine all day, or feel very unwell. A kidney infection can lead to sepsis. Pregnant women with these signs need urgent care. See our guide on clinic or emergency department . Always see a doctor rather than relying on self-care if you are a man, pregnant, a child, aged 65 or over, have diabetes, a catheter or a weak immune system, have blood in your urine, have UTIs that keep coming back, or aren’t improving within 2 days. Urine dipstick: a quick test at the clinic for signs of infection. In younger women with typical symptoms, the diagnosis is often clear from symptoms alone. Dipsticks are less reliable in older people and people with catheters, who often have bacteria in their urine without an infection. Urine culture: sent to a lab to identify the bacteria and which antibiotics work. It is used in pregnancy, for men, for repeat infections, kidney infections, and when treatment hasn’t worked. How to give a clean (mid-stream) urine sample: wash your hands, pass the first part of the urine into the toilet, catch the middle part in the sterile container without stopping the flow, then finish in the toilet. Hand it in within 2 hours, or keep it in the fridge. Give the sample before starting antibiotics if possible. Antibiotics: a simple bladder infection in a woman is usually treated with a 3 to 5 day course . Under the Ministry of Health’s national antimicrobial guideline, preferred options include nitrofurantoin and amoxicillin-clavulanate, with cephalosporins or a single dose of fosfomycin as alternatives. The choice depends on your history, kidney function and whether you are pregnant. Kidney infections need longer treatment, and sometimes a drip in hospital. Antibiotic resistance is rising. The guideline advises against some older antibiotics for UTIs because more than 30% of local E. coli are now resistant to them, and resistance to ciprofloxacin rose from about 25% in 2019 to 30% in 2023. Don’t buy antibiotics without a prescription or use leftover tablets. In Malaysia, antibiotics are prescription medicines, and the wrong antibiotic or too short a course can lead to a kidney infection or resistant bacteria. Most people feel better within 1 to 2 days of starting the right antibiotic. Finish the course, and go back if you aren’t improving after 48 hours. Bacteria in the urine without symptoms usually aren’t treated, except in pregnancy, where antenatal clinics screen for and treat them. Self-care while you recover: Drink enough water to keep your urine pale. Take paracetamol for pain. Ibuprofen is an alternative for a simple bladder infection, but avoid it with a kidney infection unless a doctor advises. Rest, and don’t hold in urine. Cystitis sachets and cranberry drinks don’t treat an active infection. A GP can test your urine and choose the right antibiotic for you. Recurrent UTI means 2 or more in 6 months, or 3 or more in a year. These steps can help: Drink enough water through the day, and pass urine when you need to rather than holding it. Pass urine soon after sex. Wipe from front to back after using the toilet. Avoid spermicides, and treat constipation. Cranberry products: a 2023 Cochrane review of 50 trials found they reduced UTIs by about a quarter in women with recurrent UTIs, and in children. They didn’t help older people in care homes or pregnant women. Avoid them if you take warfarin. After the menopause , vaginal oestrogen cream or pessaries reduce repeat UTIs. Ask your doctor. D-mannose supplements are popular, but a large 2024 trial found no benefit over placebo. For frequent infections, a doctor may suggest a non-antibiotic preventive medicine (methenamine), a low-dose antibiotic at night for several months, or a single dose after sex, and may check for an underlying cause with a scan. UTIs are less common in men and are always worth checking, as they can involve the prostate or point to a problem with bladder emptying. Kencing tak lawas , the feeling that the bladder hasn’t emptied fully, with a weak stream, dribbling and getting up at night to pass urine, is often due to an enlarged prostate (benign prostatic hyperplasia) rather than infection. About 1 in 6 Malaysian men aged 40 and over has it, rising to 1 in 3 at 75 and over. It can be treated, so see a doctor. Being unable to pass urine at all is an emergency. What are the symptoms of a UTI? Pain or burning when passing urine, needing to go often or urgently, cloudy or bloody urine and lower tummy pain. Older people may become confused instead. Can a UTI go away on its own? A mild bladder infection in a healthy woman sometimes clears by itself, but see a doctor if symptoms are severe, don’t improve in 2 days, or you are in a group that always needs a doctor. How long does a UTI take to clear with antibiotics? Most people feel better within 1 to 2 days, and a simple bladder infection is usually treated for 3 to 5 days. What are the signs of a kidney infection? Fever, shivering, pain in the back or side below the ribs, and nausea or vomiting, often with UTI symptoms. See a doctor the same day. Can I buy antibiotics for a UTI at a pharmacy in Malaysia? No. Antibiotics are prescription medicines in Malaysia. A pharmacist can advise on pain relief and when to see a doctor. Does cranberry juice help a UTI? It doesn’t treat an active infection. Cranberry products may modestly reduce repeat UTIs in some women and children. Is a UTI in pregnancy dangerous? It needs prompt treatment, as it can spread to the kidneys and affect the pregnancy. Pregnant women are also screened for bacteria in the urine at antenatal checks. What is kencing tak lawas? The feeling that your bladder hasn’t emptied fully. In men it is often due to an enlarged prostate rather than infection. See a doctor to find the cause.

title: Piles (buasir): symptoms, internal vs external, treatment and when bleeding is serious
desc: Most piles (buasir) settle within days with more fibre, water and less straining. What internal, external and “prolapsed” piles are, what helps, the treatments a doctor can offer, and why bleeding from the bottom should be checked, especially after 40.
headings: What are piles (buasir)? · Symptoms of piles (tanda buasir) · What causes piles? (Punca buasir) · When bleeding could be something serious · How to treat piles at home · Piles creams and medicines (ubat buasir) · Treatment at a clinic or hospital · Piles in pregnancy and after childbirth
keywords: Guides Piles (buasir) Haemorrhoids Buasir Rectal bleeding mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal kecemasan emergency a&e hospital klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Internal piles sit inside the back passage and are usually painless but can bleed. External piles sit under the skin around the anus and can itch and hurt. Typical signs are bright red blood on the tissue or in the toilet after a bowel movement, itching, mucus, and a soft lump at the anus. Most piles improve within a week with more fibre (25–38 g a day), plenty of water, not straining, and warm sitz baths. Piles that keep coming back can be treated in a clinic with banding, without an operation. Surgery is for large piles that stay outside. See a doctor about any bleeding from the bottom if you are over 40, if your bowel habit has changed, if the blood is dark, or if you are losing weight or feel tired. These can be signs of bowel cancer. Everyone has cushions of blood vessels in the anal canal. They become piles when they swell and stretch, usually because of pressure from straining. Internal piles (buasir dalam) form inside the back passage. They are usually painless , because the lining there has few pain nerves, but they can bleed and can slip out (prolapse). External piles (buasir luar) form under the skin around the anus. They can itch, feel sore and sometimes bleed. A thrombosed external pile is one with a blood clot inside. It appears suddenly as a very painful, purple or bluish lump. The clot stays in the pile and doesn’t travel elsewhere in the body. The four grades of internal piles Grade What happens Grade 1 Stays inside, may bleed Grade 2 Comes out when you pass stool, then goes back by itself Grade 3 Comes out ( buasir terkeluar ) and has to be pushed back with a finger Grade 4 Stays outside and can’t be pushed back bright red blood on the toilet paper, on the surface of the stool or dripping into the toilet after a bowel movement itching or irritation around the anus a soft lump at or outside the anus mucus in your underwear or on the toilet paper a feeling that you still need to go after emptying your bowels pain, mainly with external or thrombosed piles Other conditions cause similar symptoms. An anal fissure (a small tear) causes sharp pain during and after passing stool, often with a little bright blood. An abscess causes a painful swelling with fever. A doctor can usually tell the difference with a quick examination. straining on the toilet, often because of constipation from a low-fibre diet or not drinking enough sitting on the toilet for a long time, for example scrolling on a phone long-term diarrhoea pregnancy and childbirth being overweight regular heavy lifting getting older, as the supporting tissue weakens Piles are the most common cause of bright red bleeding, but not the only one. Bowel (colorectal) cancer can also cause bleeding, and in Malaysia it is often found late. In a National Cancer Registry study of more than 5,600 patients, about 7 in 10 were diagnosed at stage 3 or 4, and doctors report that symptoms in younger adults are often dismissed as piles. See a doctor soon if you have bleeding from the bottom and: you are 40 or over , or have a family history of bowel cancer your bowel habit has changed , such as looser stools or constipation that lasts several weeks the blood is dark red or black , or mixed into the stool you are losing weight without trying, feel very tired or breathless (signs of anaemia), or have tummy pain or a lump the bleeding continues after your piles have been treated The doctor may examine your bottom and arrange a colonoscopy to look inside the bowel. See our guide to bowel cancer symptoms and free screening . Go to a hospital emergency department if you are passing a lot of blood or large clots, the bleeding won’t stop, or you feel faint. See our guide on clinic or emergency department . Most piles get better within a few days to a week with simple steps, and these also help stop them coming back: Eat more fibre: aim for 25–38 g a day from vegetables, fruit, oats, wholemeal bread, brown rice, beans and lentils. Increase it gradually. A fibre supplement such as psyllium (ispaghula) helps if your diet falls short. Drink plenty of water so stools stay soft. Don’t strain , go when you feel the urge, and don’t sit on the toilet for more than a few minutes. Leave your phone outside. Sitz bath: sit in a few inches of warm (not hot) water for 10–20 minutes, once or several times a day, especially after a bowel movement. It soothes pain and itching. Keep the area clean with water and pat it dry rather than rubbing with dry tissue. Use a cold compress wrapped in a cloth for swelling. Pain relief: paracetamol is usually fine. Avoid painkillers containing codeine, which cause constipation, and avoid ibuprofen if your piles are bleeding. Vegetables, fruit and wholegrains add the fibre that keeps stools soft and stops straining. Creams, ointments and suppositories from a pharmacy can ease itching, pain and swelling for a short time. Some contain a mild steroid or a local anaesthetic. Don’t use steroid products for more than a week unless a doctor tells you to, as they can thin the skin. Flavonoid tablets (also called phlebotonics, such as micronised purified flavonoid fraction) are widely used in Malaysia. A Cochrane review found they reduced bleeding and itching, although the trials were of limited quality. Laxatives that soften the stool, such as fibre supplements, help if you are constipated. Check the product is registered. Medicines and traditional or herbal products sold in Malaysia must be registered with the National Pharmaceutical Regulatory Agency (NPRA) and carry a MAL number . Unregistered products, often sold online with promises of “piles shrinking in days”, have been found to contain hidden prescription drugs. You can check a product on the NPRA website. If piles keep bleeding or coming out despite home treatment, a doctor may refer you to a surgeon: Treatment What it involves Usually for Rubber band ligation (banding) A tight band placed around the base of the pile, which drops off within about a week. Done while you are awake, with no cuts Grade 1 to 3 internal piles Injection (sclerotherapy) or infrared coagulation An injection or heat to shrink the pile, done while you are awake Small internal piles Haemorrhoidectomy An operation to cut the piles away, usually under general anaesthetic Grade 3 and 4 piles, or large internal and external piles Haemorrhoidal artery ligation or stapling Operations that cut off the blood supply to the piles or lift them back into place Selected cases; less pain, but piles come back more often Recovery after a haemorrhoidectomy usually takes 2 to 4 weeks, and the first bowel movements are the most painful. Stool softeners and sitz baths help. A thrombosed external pile that is very painful can be cut open to remove the clot if you are seen within about 2 to 3 days. After that, it usually settles on its own within a couple of weeks. Piles can come back after any treatment, so the fibre, water and no-straining habits still matter. Piles are common in late pregnancy and after giving birth, because of pressure from the baby, hormones, constipation and pushing during labour. In one study of 280 pregnant women, more than 4 in 10 developed piles or a similar problem, mostly in the third trimester or after delivery. Eat plenty of fibre, drink water and stay active to prevent constipation. Use a cold compress or sitz bath for comfort. Check with your doctor, midwife or pharmacist before using any cream or tablet. Piles that start in pregnancy often improve within weeks of the birth. What is buasir in English? Buasir is piles, also called haemorrhoids (or hemorrhoids in American English): swollen blood vessels in and around the anus. What are the signs of piles? Bright red blood after a bowel movement, itching, mucus, a soft lump at the anus and, with external piles, pain. How long do piles take to go away? Mild piles often settle within a few days to a week with more fibre, water and less straining. A thrombosed external pile can take a couple of weeks. What is the difference between internal and external piles? Internal piles are inside the back passage and usually painless but may bleed or slip out. External piles are under the skin around the anus and can itch and hurt. Can piles turn into cancer? No, piles don’t turn into cancer. But bowel cancer can cause similar bleeding, so see a doctor about bleeding if you are 40 or over or have other warning signs. Do piles need surgery? Most don’t. Piles that keep bleeding or prolapsing can often be treated with banding in a clinic. Surgery is mainly for large piles that stay outside. Is a sitz bath good for piles? Many people find a warm sitz bath for 10–20 minutes soothes pain and itching, although the evidence for it is limited. Which ubat buasir can I buy at a pharmacy? Pharmacies sell creams, suppositories, fibre supplements and flavonoid tablets for piles. Ask the pharmacist, use steroid creams for no more than a week, and choose products with a MAL registration number.

title: Scabies (kudis buta): symptoms, how it spreads, treatment and stopping it coming back
desc: Scabies (kudis buta) is an intensely itchy rash caused by tiny mites. It spreads through close skin contact, often through whole families and hostels. How to recognise it, how to use the treatment properly, why everyone at home must be treated at once, and why the itch lingers.
headings: What is scabies (kudis buta)? · How scabies spreads · Symptoms of scabies · Complications · Scabies treatment (ubat kudis buta) · Treat everyone at the same time · Cleaning bedding, clothes and the home · After treatment: the itch, and when to go back
keywords: Aesthetics & skin Scabies (kudis buta) Scabies Kudis buta Sarcoptes scabiei mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Scabies is caused by the Sarcoptes scabiei mite. It spreads mainly through prolonged skin-to-skin contact, such as sharing a bed, and only sometimes through bedding or clothes. The itch is worst at night. Look for small bumps and thin, wavy lines (burrows) between the fingers, on the wrists, elbows, armpits, waist, buttocks and genitals. The first-choice treatment in Malaysia is permethrin 5% cream, applied to the whole body from the jawline down, left on for 8–12 hours, and repeated after 1 week. Everyone at home and other close contacts must be treated on the same day, even without symptoms, or the mites spread back. The itch can last 1–2 weeks or more after successful treatment. That doesn’t mean the treatment failed. Scabies is a skin infestation by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei , which is too small to see with the naked eye. Female mites burrow into the top layer of skin to lay eggs. The intense itch is an allergic reaction to the mites, their eggs and their waste. Scabies is common worldwide, with at least 200 million people affected at any time. In Malaysia, outbreaks are most often seen where people live closely together, such as large households, hostels, welfare homes and detention centres. In early 2026, for example, the Kelantan Health Department reported 279 cases among Orang Asli communities in Gua Musang since the start of 2025. It is linked to crowding and close contact, not to being dirty. Anyone can get it. Prolonged skin-to-skin contact is the main route: sharing a bed, cuddling and caring for children, and sexual contact. A quick handshake or hug is unlikely to pass it on. Bedding, towels and clothes are a less common route, because mites survive only 2 to 3 days off the skin. They matter more with crusted scabies (see below). If it is your first time , symptoms take 2 to 6 weeks to appear, but you can pass it on during that time. If you have had scabies before, itching starts within 1 to 5 days. Pets don’t spread human scabies. Animal mange is caused by a different mite, which may cause a brief itch in people but doesn’t settle in human skin. Intense itching, worst at night , and often several people in the home itching at once Burrows: short, thin, wavy grey or silvery lines a rash of small red bumps or blisters, and scratch marks Where it appears in adults and older children: between the fingers, the wrists, elbows, armpit folds, around the nipples, the waist and belly button, the buttocks, and the penis and scrotum. The head and neck are usually spared. In babies and young children , scabies can also affect the face, scalp, neck, palms and soles, and may cause small blisters. Itchy lumps (nodules) can last for weeks or months after treatment. Crusted (Norwegian) scabies is a severe form with thick, crusted skin and huge numbers of mites. It is very contagious. It mainly affects older people, people with a weak immune system, and people with conditions that limit sensation or movement. It may itch surprisingly little, and needs a doctor’s care. Scabies often spreads through families, so everyone in the home is treated at the same time. Scratching breaks the skin and lets bacteria in, causing impetigo (crusted sores), boils, cellulitis and, rarely, blood infection. Some of these bacteria can damage the kidneys. See a doctor if sores are spreading, weeping yellow fluid or very painful, or if you have a fever. You may need antibiotics as well as scabies treatment. Under the Ministry of Health’s scabies guideline, the first choice for most people is permethrin 5% cream . Other options include benzyl benzoate lotion, sulphur ointment for young babies, and oral ivermectin tablets for some cases. A doctor will choose the right one, especially for babies, pregnant women and crusted scabies. How to apply permethrin cream properly: Apply it at bedtime to cool, dry skin , not straight after a hot bath. Cover the whole body from the jawline down , not just the itchy areas: between the fingers and toes, under the nails, the armpits, the genitals, the buttocks and the soles of the feet. Ask someone to help with your back. For babies and young children, the doctor may also advise treating the face and scalp, avoiding the eyes and mouth. Leave it on for 8 to 12 hours , usually overnight, then wash it off. If you wash your hands during that time, apply more to your hands . Repeat after 1 week to kill any mites that hatched from eggs. Ask a pharmacist or doctor how much cream you need for everyone at home. Antihistamine tablets and a soothing moisturiser can help with the itch. Home remedies (petua) such as soaking in salt water may soothe the skin for a while, but they don’t kill the mites. Scabies needs a scabies treatment. This is the most common reason scabies keeps coming back. Everyone in your household , your sexual partners and anyone else who has had prolonged skin contact with you in the past 2 months should be treated on the same day , even if they have no rash or itch. Remember, symptoms can take up to 6 weeks to appear. In hostels, schools and care homes, the District Health Office can help organise treatment for everyone at once. On the day you start treatment: Wash bedding, towels and clothes used in the past 3 days in hot water (above 50°C) , and dry them in a hot dryer or in the sun. Items you can’t wash, such as soft toys or shoes, can be sealed in a plastic bag for at least 3 days , after which the mites die. Vacuum mattresses, sofas and carpets. You don’t need to fumigate or spray insecticide around the home. Itching often continues for 1 to 2 weeks , sometimes up to 4 weeks, after successful treatment, as the skin reacts to dead mites. This doesn’t mean you need more cream. Using it too often can irritate the skin. See your doctor again if new burrows or bumps appear, or the itch is no better after 2 to 4 weeks. The usual reasons treatment fails are missing parts of the body, not repeating after a week, or someone at home not being treated. School and work: children and adults can usually go back 24 hours after the first treatment . For other causes of itchy skin, such as eczema, hives and fungal rashes, see our guide to itchy skin . What is kudis buta in English? Kudis buta is scabies, an itchy skin infestation caused by the Sarcoptes scabiei mite. What causes kudis buta? Tiny mites that burrow into the skin. They spread mainly through prolonged skin-to-skin contact, such as sharing a bed, and less often through bedding or clothes. It isn’t caused by poor hygiene. How long does scabies take to go away? The mites are usually killed by two treatments a week apart, but the itch can carry on for 1 to 2 weeks, and sometimes up to 4 weeks, afterwards. How do I use permethrin cream for scabies? Apply it to cool, dry skin over the whole body from the jawline down, including between the fingers and toes and under the nails. Leave it on for 8 to 12 hours, wash it off, and repeat after 1 week. Does my family need treatment too? Yes. Everyone in the household and other close contacts should be treated on the same day, even without symptoms, or the scabies is likely to come back. Can scabies go away on its own? No. Without treatment the mites keep breeding, the rash spreads and others get infected. Can I go to work or school with scabies? You can usually go back 24 hours after the first treatment. Does soaking in salt water cure scabies? No. It may soothe the skin, but it doesn’t kill the mites. You need a scabies treatment such as permethrin cream.

title: mySalam 2026: who qualifies, how to check (semakan), benefits and how to claim
desc: mySalam gives STR recipients and their spouses free protection: RM8,000 if diagnosed with one of 50 critical illnesses, RM50 a day for government hospital stays, and help with medical devices. Who qualifies, how to check, and how to make a claim without it being rejected.
headings: What is mySalam? · Who qualifies for mySalam in 2026? · mySalam benefits · How to check your mySalam status (semakan) · How to make a mySalam claim · Why mySalam claims are rejected · mySalam in numbers · mySalam, PeKa B40 and MediAsas compared
keywords: Guides mySalam mySalam Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah Takaful kencing manis gula hba1c darah tinggi hypertension bp tekanan darah klinik doctor doktor gp saringan check-up checkup medical
body: mySalam covers STR recipients aged 18 to 65 and their spouses. Enrolment is automatic through STR data, so there is no registration and no contribution. It pays RM8,000 once if you are diagnosed with one of 50 critical illnesses, including cancer, heart attack, stroke and, since 2025, some mental illnesses. It also pays RM50 a day when you are admitted to a government hospital, for up to 14 days (RM700) a year, and helps with some medical devices. You claim online on the mySalam portal or at mySalam kiosks in government hospitals. Missing documents are the main reason claims are rejected. About 1.88 million people had received mySalam payouts by the end of 2025, totalling RM1.42 billion. mySalam is a national health protection scheme launched in 2019 for the B40 (lower-income) group. It is funded through a trust fund managed by the Ministry of Finance and administered by Great Eastern Takaful Berhad. It doesn’t pay your medical bills. Instead it gives you cash when you are diagnosed with a serious illness or admitted to hospital, to help with lost income and other costs. It is separate from PeKa B40 , which offers free health screening and other help for STR recipients aged 40 and over, and from MediAsas , the voluntary medical insurance plan starting in January 2027. STR recipients aged 18 to 65 , and their spouses , are covered. About 9.15 million STR recipients are eligible in 2026. Coverage is automatic. mySalam uses the STR records from the Inland Revenue Board (LHDN), so you don’t need to register or pay anything. If you don’t receive STR , you aren’t covered. If you think you qualify for STR but haven’t applied, apply for STR first through LHDN. Coverage follows your STR status for the year, so check your status each year rather than assuming you are still covered. Benefit What you get Critical illness RM8,000 , paid once, if you are diagnosed with one of 50 listed critical illnesses Hospital income RM50 a day when you are admitted to a government hospital, up to 14 days ( RM700 ) a year Medical devices Help with the cost of some medical devices, such as heart stents, of up to RM30,000 The 50 critical illnesses include common conditions such as cancer, heart attack, stroke and kidney failure. From 2025, the list was expanded from 45 to 50 illnesses, adding conditions including schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and major depressive disorder , thalassaemia major, aplastic anaemia, psoriasis, pemphigus vulgaris, rheumatoid arthritis and some rare diseases. The full list is on the mySalam website. The hospital income is paid for stays in government hospitals, which reports describe as including military and university hospitals. It is not paid for private hospital stays. Go to the official mySalam website at www.mysalam.com.my . Choose the eligibility check ( semakan kelayakan ) and enter your MyKad number . The result shows whether you are covered for the year. “mySalam login” refers to your account on the same website, which you sign in to with your MyKad number. You use it to check your status, submit claims, follow a claim and update your bank details. Beware of fakes. mySalam is free. Use only the official website, and never pay anyone or share your banking password to “register” or speed up a claim. You make the claim yourself. The hospital doesn’t submit it for you. You can claim: online through your account on the mySalam website, or at a mySalam kiosk : there are more than 140 in government hospitals. Documents you need: Claim Documents Critical illness The mySalam critical illness form completed by your doctor, and a copy of the front and back of your MyKad Hospital income Your hospital discharge note, and a copy of the front and back of your MyKad Upload clear PDF or JPEG copies. Approved payments go into the bank account registered in your mySalam account, so make sure your details are correct. Deadline: claims have had to be submitted by 30 June of the following year . For example, 2025 claims were due by 30 June 2026. Check the website for the current deadline and claim as soon as you can. A November 2025 report found that only about 54% of claims made from 2019 to 2024 were paid. Common problems include: missing or unclear documents , such as a blurry discharge note or an incomplete doctor’s form an illness that isn’t on the list of 50, or doesn’t meet its definition a stay in a private hospital, which isn’t covered for hospital income not being an STR recipient, or the spouse of one, in that year a claim sent after the deadline If your claim is rejected for missing documents, collect them and claim again before the deadline. For a critical illness claim, ask your doctor to complete the mySalam form when you are diagnosed. According to figures given by the government in June 2026, by 31 December 2025: about 1.29 million people had received hospital income payouts, totalling RM394.9 million 89,085 people had received critical illness payouts, totalling RM712.7 million 13,128 people had received medical device help, totalling RM65.3 million In all, about 1.88 million people had received RM1.42 billion. The scheme was extended into 2026 in Budget 2026, and the Budget 2027 speech in October 2026 said it will continue in 2027. mySalam PeKa B40 MediAsas Who STR recipients aged 18–65 and spouses STR recipients aged 40+ and spouses Anyone who signs up (from January 2027) Cost Free, automatic Free Paid premium; EPF savings can be used What it gives Cash for critical illness and government hospital stays; medical device help Free screening, medical device aid, cancer treatment and transport incentives Medical insurance for hospital treatment If you qualify for both mySalam and PeKa B40, you can use both. PeKa B40’s free screening, at a panel clinic, can pick up conditions such as diabetes, high blood pressure and some cancers early. See our guide to free health screening in Malaysia . Who is eligible for mySalam? STR recipients aged 18 to 65 and their spouses. Coverage is automatic through STR records, with no registration or payment. How do I check if I am covered by mySalam? Enter your MyKad number in the eligibility check on the official mySalam website, www.mysalam.com.my. How much does mySalam pay? RM8,000 once for one of 50 critical illnesses, RM50 a day for government hospital stays up to RM700 a year, and help of up to RM30,000 with some medical devices. What is the mySalam RM700? It is the yearly maximum for hospital income: RM50 a day for up to 14 days in a government hospital. Does mySalam cover private hospitals? The hospital income benefit is for stays in government hospitals, including military and university hospitals, not private hospitals. How do I claim mySalam? Online through your account on the mySalam website, or at a mySalam kiosk in a government hospital. You need your doctor’s critical illness form or your discharge note, plus a copy of your MyKad. Is mySalam continuing in 2027? Yes. The Budget 2027 speech in October 2026 said mySalam will continue in 2027. Do I need to pay or register for mySalam? No. It is free and automatic for eligible STR recipients and their spouses. Don’t pay anyone who offers to register you.

title: Syphilis (sifilis) and STI testing in Malaysia: symptoms, tests, treatment and where to get checked
desc: Syphilis often starts with a painless sore that heals on its own, so many people don’t know they have it. Its stages and symptoms, how the blood tests work, the treatment, the signs of gonorrhoea and chlamydia, and where to get a confidential STI test in Malaysia.
headings: Syphilis and STIs in Malaysia · Syphilis symptoms by stage · Syphilis tests and what they mean · Syphilis treatment · Gonorrhoea and chlamydia · Where to get a confidential STI test in Malaysia · Prevention
keywords: Prevention Syphilis and STI testing Syphilis Sexually transmitted infections Gonorrhoea mengandung hamil pregnancy antenatal vaksin suntikan jab immunisation klinik doctor doktor gp aesthetic estetik kecantikan beauty kulit skin botox filler laser facial
body: Syphilis usually starts with a firm, painless sore where the infection entered, which heals by itself within 3 to 6 weeks even without treatment. Weeks later, a non-itchy rash can appear, often on the palms and soles, with fever and swollen glands. Then the infection can stay hidden for years. It is diagnosed with blood tests and cured with penicillin injections. One type of test can stay positive for life even after cure. Gonorrhoea and chlamydia often cause no symptoms, especially in women, but can cause infertility. They are found with a urine test or swab. You can get a confidential STI test at government health clinics and private GP clinics. Partners need testing and treatment too. In 2022, Malaysia recorded 4,669 new cases of syphilis and 1,819 of gonorrhoea , according to figures given to Parliament by the Health Minister. About 1 in 15 syphilis cases and more than 1 in 5 gonorrhoea cases were in people under 21. Both are notifiable diseases under the Prevention and Control of Infectious Diseases Act 1988, so doctors must report cases to the Ministry of Health, which keeps them confidential. Malaysia screens almost all pregnant women for syphilis and HIV. In October 2026 it kept its World Health Organization validation for eliminating mother-to-child transmission of both infections, which it first achieved in 2018, the first country in the Western Pacific to do so. Symptoms usually start about 3 weeks after infection, but can take anywhere from 10 days to 3 months. Stage What happens Primary A firm, round, usually painless sore (chancre) on the penis, vagina, anus or mouth. It is easy to miss and heals by itself in 3 to 6 weeks, but the infection remains. Secondary A few weeks to months later: a rash that usually doesn’t itch , often on the palms of the hands and soles of the feet, with fever, tiredness, swollen glands, sore throat or patchy hair loss. It also clears without treatment. Latent No symptoms, sometimes for many years. Many people stay in this stage for life, but can still pass syphilis to a baby during pregnancy. Tertiary 10 to 30 years later in some untreated people: damage to the heart, brain, nerves and other organs. At any stage , syphilis can spread to the brain and nerves (neurosyphilis), the eyes or the ears. Get help urgently for sudden changes in vision or hearing, a severe headache, confusion or weakness. Syphilis is most infectious in the first two stages, through direct contact with the sore or rash during vaginal, anal or oral sex. Syphilis is diagnosed with a blood test . Two kinds are used together: Treponemal tests (such as TPHA, TPPA or an EIA test) detect antibodies to the syphilis bacterium. Once positive, they usually stay positive for life , even after successful treatment. A positive result on its own can mean a past, treated infection. Non-treponemal tests (VDRL or RPR) measure how active the infection is. The level falls after treatment, so doctors use it to check that treatment has worked. Rapid tests using a finger-prick of blood give a result within minutes, so treatment can sometimes start on the same visit. Timing: antibodies may not show up until a few weeks after infection. If you test soon after a risk and the result is negative, the doctor may ask you to repeat it later. If you have a sore, the doctor may also test the sore itself. Anyone with syphilis should also be tested for HIV, as the two often go together. See our guide to HIV testing, PrEP and treatment . Under the Ministry of Health’s antibiotic guideline: Early syphilis (infected within about the past 2 years) is treated with a single injection of benzathine penicillin . Late or latent syphilis of unknown duration needs one injection a week for 3 weeks . People allergic to penicillin can take doxycycline tablets for 2 to 4 weeks, except in pregnancy, when penicillin is needed. Neurosyphilis is treated in hospital with penicillin through a drip. Some people get a fever, headache and aches within a day of the first injection, as the bacteria die. This settles within a day and isn’t an allergy. After treatment: Don’t have sex until you and your partner have finished treatment and the sore or rash has gone. The NHS advises waiting 2 weeks after treatment ends. Go back for repeat blood tests , usually at 6 and 12 months, to make sure the infection has cleared. Recent sexual partners need testing and treatment, even if they feel well. The clinic can help you tell them. Treatment doesn’t make you immune. You can catch syphilis again. These are the other common bacterial STIs. Both are often silent , especially in women. Gonorrhoea (kencing nanah) Chlamydia Typical symptoms Pus-like discharge from the penis and burning when passing urine in men. Most women have no symptoms, or unusual discharge. Often none. Sometimes discharge, burning when passing urine, bleeding after sex or pain in the testicles. Test Urine test for men, or a swab, which women can often take themselves Urine test or swab Treatment An antibiotic injection (ceftriaxone) A course of antibiotic tablets Untreated, both can cause pelvic inflammatory disease , ectopic pregnancy and infertility , and can be passed to a baby at birth. Throat and rectal infections are common and usually cause no symptoms, so tell the doctor what kind of sex you have had, so they can test the right places. Gonorrhoea is becoming resistant to antibiotics , including in Southeast Asia. Don’t take leftover antibiotics or buy them without a prescription: see a doctor and go back for a test of cure if advised. Government health clinics (Klinik Kesihatan): outpatient fees for Malaysians are very low. Many clinics test for syphilis and HIV, and some offer free HIV PrEP. Private GP clinics: you can usually be seen quickly, including in the evening. Ask for an “STI screen” and say which infections you want tested. Community and NGO clinics offer testing and support in some cities, and HIV self-test kits are sold at pharmacies. Confidentiality: doctors must keep your medical information confidential. Notifying the Ministry of Health is for public health and isn’t shared with your employer or family. Who should test, and when: anyone with symptoms such as a sore, rash, discharge or burning after condomless sex with a new or casual partner if a partner has an STI at least yearly if you have several partners, and every 3 to 6 months for men who have sex with men at higher risk in pregnancy, at the first antenatal visit, which is routine in Malaysia A full STI screen usually means a blood test for syphilis and HIV, plus a urine test or swabs for gonorrhoea and chlamydia. Use condoms every time, for vaginal, anal and oral sex. They greatly reduce, but don’t remove, the risk of syphilis, as sores can be on skin a condom doesn’t cover. Test regularly if you have new or several partners, and encourage partners to test. HIV PrEP prevents HIV but not other STIs, so regular STI testing is part of PrEP care. In May 2026 the World Health Organization recommended doxy-PEP , a dose of doxycycline after sex, for some men who have sex with men and transgender women at high risk. It isn’t part of Ministry of Health policy in Malaysia, so discuss it with a doctor rather than self-medicating. The hepatitis B and HPV vaccines protect against two other sexually transmitted infections. See our guides to hepatitis B and the HPV vaccine . What are the first signs of syphilis? Usually a firm, painless sore on the genitals, anus or mouth about 3 weeks after infection. It heals on its own, but the infection remains and needs treatment. What does a syphilis rash look like? A rash that usually doesn’t itch, often on the palms and soles, sometimes with fever, swollen glands and patchy hair loss. It appears weeks to months after the sore. Can syphilis be cured? Yes. Penicillin injections cure syphilis. Damage already done in late syphilis may not reverse, which is why early testing matters. What does a positive TPHA test mean? It shows you have had syphilis at some point. It usually stays positive for life, even after cure, so doctors use it together with a VDRL or RPR test to tell whether the infection is active. Where can I get an STI test in Malaysia? At government health clinics, private GP clinics and some community clinics. Testing is confidential. What are the symptoms of gonorrhoea (kencing nanah)? Men often have pus-like discharge and burning when passing urine. Most women have no symptoms. It is diagnosed with a urine test or swab. Can I have chlamydia without symptoms? Yes, most people with chlamydia have no symptoms. Untreated, it can cause infertility, so test after condomless sex with a new partner. Do I need to tell my partner? Yes. Recent partners need testing and treatment, or you can be reinfected. The clinic can help you tell them.
